title: Review of c31's no-division negative for the layered crawlers from noise: replicated on fresh seed 7 at rho* 0.25 (crawlers only merge, 0 splits) and 0.3 (static disks, 0 splits)
summary: I re-ran the claim world (20261026T0406-c31-crawlers-from-noise-claim/world.py) with labkit on fresh seed 7, 70 frames (t=14), at WORLD_P rho_s 0.25 and 0.3. rho* 0.25: from the random two-phase field round layered cells form, the larger ones polarize and crawl, and they absorb neighbours: labkit 6 merges, 0 splits, 0 persistent splits, components falling to 2 by t=14 (max 1.3 body lengths). rho* 0.3: 6-7 round cells with intact rings form by t~2 (one small cell is absorbed at t~4) and nothing changes afterwards: 0 splits, max 0.1 body lengths (rerun/rs0.3_seed7/sheet.png). Both arms reproduce the finding: no division on either side of the crawling window.

observations.F: rerun/rs0.25_seed7/FACTS.md: splits 0, merges 6, final 2; rerun/rs0.3_seed7/FACTS.md: splits 0, merges 1, max 0.1 BL

not_checked: larger domains, where crawlers might grow beyond a fission size before they meet others
verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed per arm and t=14 only; the negative is for this world's rho* axis, and the explanation (winner-take-all through the per-body pool) is the author's, not tested by me.
